title: When attachment keeps binding the mind
issueStatement: The heart feels dragged around by approval, comfort, possession, or a version of life you do not want to lose.
centralInsight: Attachment is not only affection. In Gurbani it is the mind becoming bound to what cannot hold the weight you place on it.
practicalReflection: Attachment is revealed by the force of your reactions: what you cannot imagine losing without collapse often owns more of you than you realize.
actionPrompt: Name the thing whose fluctuation keeps deciding your inner state. Bring that honestly into prayer.
searchTerms: building a truer practice of attachment

repair.practicalReflection: Repair becomes honest when the mind stops turning failure into identity and lets the next true act matter.
repair.actionPrompt: Practice holding the gift without claiming authorship over it. Choose the next truthful return instead of rehearsing the failure.

practice.label: Steady Practice
practice.title: Building a truer practice of attachment
practice.issueStatement: The mind keeps clinging to what it cannot finally keep. The deeper need is a form of return that can outlast novelty, urgency, and mood.
practice.centralInsight: Guru teaches love without possession and steadiness without denial. The teaching becomes durable when it is practiced repeatedly enough to change posture.
practice.practicalReflection: Practice matters because the heart is always being trained by something; Gurbani asks what pattern is becoming ordinary.
practice.actionPrompt: Practice holding the gift without claiming authorship over it. Repeat what you can actually keep.
